notes: 4x AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, RDNA4, 32 GiB, identical GPUs) shared host. Served with vLLM in a locally patched derivative of ghcr.io/inferstation/vllm-rocm-r9700-main (digest above): the base image ships transformers 5.13.0 while the bundled vLLM hunyuan_vl image processor still calls the transformers 4.x AutoImageProcessor.register(str, class) API, which aborts model-architecture inspection; the one-line registration was ported to the transformers 5.x config-class API (HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1, --trust-remote-code). Speed is measured on a single GPU (HIP index 3, port 18021), one visible GPU, TP=1, request concurrency=1, torch.compile enabled, with --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN. TRITON_ATTN is the decisive serving flag on gfx1201/RDNA4: the default ROCM_ATTN decode kernel scales poorly with KV length, so the ~3,500 vision-token context per OCR page roughly halves decode; forcing --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN removes that penalty and raises concurrency-1 decode ~3x (89 -> 267 tok/s on quick9-c1), reproducibly and with identical model, weights and generation parameters (AITER/flash_attn are unavailable on gfx1201, so ROCM_ATTN and TRITON_ATTN are the only decoder options). Accuracy is not a speed measurement: it is distributed over two independent TP=1 enforce-eager replicas on HIP indices 3 (port 18017) and 2 (port 18018) driven with multi-stream client concurrency for throughput; enforce-eager avoids per-image-shape recompilation across the 1651 variable-resolution pages. The published accuracy (Overall 95.62) was scored on those default-ROCM_ATTN replicas; TRITON_ATTN differs only by floating-point rounding near EOS (a 9-token drift over the 27 quick9 requests, outputs ~99.9% identical), so an accuracy re-score under TRITON_ATTN is expected within noise but was not separately published. HIP index 1 was excluded due to a competing workload. Generation parameters match the protocol (max_tokens=32768, repetition_penalty=1.08, temperature=0, top_k=-1) with the pinned batch_infer streaming repetition guard.
